exposure: Women who were underweight or normal weight in the first pregnancy
Women who maintained a healthy BMI category in both pregnancies
cohort: 15,108 women who delivered their first two nonanomalous singleton live births in Missouri (1989-2005) and experienced preeclampsia in the first pregnancy
finding: Interpregnancy weight gain was associated with increased risk of recurrent preeclampsia, LGA, and cesarean delivery, while interpregnancy weight loss was associated with increased risk of SGA and, in some cases, reduced risk of recurrent preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Interpregnancy weight gain was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
